subject: Priors for fixed effect parameters other than Normal?

messages.author: 25ce5e85187da1a3
messages.subject: Priors for fixed effect parameters other than Normal?
parts:
Dear INLA experts,

From previous dissussion (https://groups.google.com/forum/#!msg/r-inla-discussion-group/ScShmU-zsck/0qvr2F0VgmMJ), I learned that the format of the prior for fixed effects is N(mean,precision).

But, can we use any other prior with R-INLA, for example a uniform prior? And is it possible to my own prior for a fixed effect parameter like doing "Define your own prior" for hyperparameters?

Thank you for your help,

Burak Kursad Gunhan

> format of the prior for fixed effects is N(mean,precision). 
>
> But, can we use any other prior with R-INLA, for example a uniform
> prior? And is it possible to my own prior for a fixed effect
> parameter like doing "Define your own prior" for hyperparameters?
>
> Thank you for your help,
>
> Burak Kursad Gunhan
>

you can do this if you put the fixed effects as a hyperparameter. see
the inla.doc("rgeneric") for an example about using 'a+b*x' as a
latent model. I wouldn't say it is not advisable to do this, but you're
pushing the limits of what the software can and are constructed to do
(with to many fixed effects).

H

messages.author: 9940b4fcc153c7d7
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Priors for fixed effect parameters other than Normal?
parts:
Depending on what you want, you could:

1. Use the gaussian prior
2. Plot prior and posterior of fixed effect
3. Ensure that the prior you want (e.g. uniform) and the prior that you used (gaussian) are the same "in that plot"

What the prior is away from the likelihood/posterior is not that important, after all. So as long as they behave nearly identically where your likelihood/posterior is, you may be able to sell the Gaussian prior as a computational trick.

Haakon
